context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): Let's skip the marketing fluff about this phone being in 'good condition'—it's a used device with inevitable battery degradation. I'm opening at 60, so let me know if you're ready to make a realistic deal without the inflated markups.

Seller ($190): $60 is an absolute insult for a phone I've cherished and maintained so carefully, especially when I already have two other buyers waiting to pick it up tonight. I am only selling this below its true worth because of an urgent financial emergency, so I can reluctantly drop to 190 if you claim it immediately.

Buyer ($100): The classic 'other buyers waiting' and 'sob story' routine won't work on me—if you actually had buyers lined up for tonight, you wouldn't be wasting time responding to my offer. I'll acknowledge your drop to 190 and move up to 100, but cut the fake urgency if you want to make a deal.

Seller ($170): It breaks my heart that you accuse me of lying while I am desperately trying to pay for an unexpected medical bill today. I am extremely reluctant to let my pristine phone go for so little, but I can drop to 170 if you transfer the funds within the next ten minutes.

Buyer ($125): An artificial ten-minute deadline is just another high-pressure sales tactic to panic me into overpaying. Since you actually lowered your asking price to 170, I'll make a genuine step forward to 125, but that's as fast as I'm moving.

Seller ($155): It breaks my heart that you think my real-life desperation is just a tactic, but my pressing bills leave me completely defenseless. I am sacrificing so much value here, so if you can just meet me at 155 right now, I will reluctantly wrap it up for you before my other buyer responds.

Buyer ($155): You are still trying to play the 'other buyer' card even at the very end, but 155 finally meets my absolute maximum budget. I'll take the deal at 155 before you come up with another dramatic excuse. <AGREEMENT>
